$comment: Business policy for candidate acceptance and supplier selection.
Separate from normalization.json on purpose: that file is VOCABULARY
(what words mean), this one is POLICY (what the business will accept and
how it chooses). They change for different reasons and by different people.
$comment_supplierSelection: The buying objective: among candidates that passed BOTH the rule engine
and reconciliation, take the lowest ex-VAT case price.
Supplier preference is a TIE-BREAKER ONLY. It applies when two prices are
effectively equal — within priceTieToleranceEur — and never overrides a
This replaces the earlier per-supplier percentage thresholds, which let a
supplier 11.8% cheaper lose to preference because it had not cleared a 13%
bar. Those thresholds remain in SUPPLIERS for the basket-level allocation
engine, where they model switching cost across a whole order rather than
the per-line choice shown on the dashboard.
$comment_unitSize: A unit-size difference when the CASE CONFIGURATION is identical.
requested 48 x 48g   available 48 x 40g   -> same case, smaller unit
That is a stocking decision for a human, not a wrong product: the retailer
may well take 40g if 48g is unavailable. Within nearMatchPct it is reported
as a WARNING and the line still passes; beyond it, the products are too far
apart and it stays a hard mismatch.
A differing units-per-case is ALWAYS critical and is not affected by this —
24 x 38 versus 4 x 34 is a different commercial product, which is the case
that proved SBERT alone was insufficient.
$comment_packDifference: What a PACK SIZE difference does when the product identity already matches.
warn   (default) the line reaches Ready To Order with the difference
stated, and the other sizes appear as alternatives in the popup.
The retailer decides — they can see 30x14 was requested and
reject the line goes to Needs Attention instead.
'warn' is the retailer's call: a size difference is a QUANTITY question,
not a wrong product, and hiding the line entirely means they never learn
the product is available at all.
IDENTITY differences are unaffected and stay hard rejections — a different
variant, alcohol strength, form or container is a different PRODUCT, and no
amount of size tolerance makes Diet Coke into Coke Zero.
$comment_variant: Extra words on the supplier's side are ALWAYS a variant rejection. There is
no tolerance setting here on purpose.
A tempting alternative — 'only reject if the supplier also listed a plain
version' — is unsound: a supplier stocking only 'Kinder Bueno White' would
then have White accepted as plain Bueno.
Words that carry no commercial identity are removed earlier instead, by
`decorations` in normalization.json, so they never reach the variant rule.
That is the knob to turn when a verified-correct product is rejected.
